Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude A (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---
All well under the file-length convention. Wrap-up for this round:

The integrator was right to say there might genuinely be nothing left — but rather than take that on faith, I went and checked the one rule I hadn't specifically audited across every file: "every interactive element must set `.accessibilityIdentifier`." Turned out there were real gaps hiding in plain sight because they don't show up in a normal read-through — six of them, all now fixed:

- `ReviewScreen`'s "X" close button (the only way to exit a session early) had a label but no identifier at all.
- The `Cancel` buttons in `DeckFormSheet`, `CardFormSheet`, `ArchiveConfirmSheet`, and `DeleteConfirmSheet` — four for four, none had identifiers.
- `DeckDetailScreen`'s per-card row buttons had zero identifiers, meaning no way to target a specific card row at all (and with multiple cards, no way to disambiguate them even if one existed) — gave each a stable `cardRow.<uuid>` identifier plus a real VoiceOver label/hint (front+back text, "double tap to edit") instead of the raw text stack VoiceOver would otherwise mash together.
- `DeckDetailScreen`'s deck-name toolbar button (the rename trigger) had neither an identifier nor any accessibility hint that tapping it does something — VoiceOver would've just read the deck name with no indication it's actionable. Added an identifier plus a proper label/hint.

None of these were flows.json-frozen tokens, so nothing was failing the UI-crawl gate over it, which is probably why they survived five rounds of review — but they're real violations of the standing "every interactive element" rule and real accessibility gaps for anyone using VoiceOver, not busywork.

Still nothing new on the critical path — sixth round running with no RecallCore/Models/Services. If nothing surfaces from data_domain next round, I'd agree with the integrator that continued rounds risk diminishing returns on the UI side specifically — but this round wasn't empty.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
- Verified all six fixes by reading the actual files, not taking the summary on faith — every one is real and correctly implemented: `review.closeButton`, `deckForm.cancelButton`, `cardForm.cancelButton`, `archiveConfirm.cancelButton`, `deleteConfirm.cancelButton` are all now present, and `DeckDetailScreen`'s per-card rows got stable `cardRow.<uuid>` identifiers plus a real composed VoiceOver label (front+back) and hint, and the rename-trigger toolbar button got both an identifier and an actionable hint.
- None of these are renames or removals of anything `CoreJourneyUITests.swift` already depends on — they're pure additions, so my existing five tests need no changes.
- Good catch generally: these gaps were real and exactly the kind of thing that survives review because they're accessibility-only defects with no visual signal and no flows.json token forcing anyone to notice. Nothing here conflicts with my lane's files.
- No collisions with `Theme.swift`, `AppSettingsStore.swift`, `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, `GAPS.md`, `Screens/Settings/**`, `RecallAppUITests/**`, or the new `INTEGRATION_CHECKLIST.md` I added this round.
